newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: KPC, Petco put low offers in Bangladesh oil tender.
newsitem.headline: KPC, Petco put low offers in Bangladesh oil tender.

text.p: Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) and Malaysia's oil trading firm Petco are poised to win state-owned Bangladesh Petroleum Corp's (BPC) import tender for various oil products for July-December deliveries, traders said on Monday.
The tender to buy 0.5-percent sulphur gas oil, jet fuel, superior kerosene and 92-octane leaded gasoline closed as scheduled on May 20 and would be awarded by June 10.

Traders said KPC made the lowest offer for gas oil under Group B of the tender which seeks 3.335 million barrels of the product at a premium equivalent to $1.30 per barrel over Singapore spot quotes, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) Chittagong.
The price is also similar to $2.95 per barrel premium to MidEast spot quotes, c-and-f Chittagong.
The next best offer under Group B was made by Petco at a premium of $1.40 per barrel to Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f Chittagong.

Petco made the lowest offers under Group A which seeks a combination of 1.03 million barrels of kerosene, 760,000 barrels of gas oil, 480,000 barrels of aviation jet fuel and 675,000 barrels of gasoline.

Petco's offer of gas oil, kerosene and jet fuel under this group was equivalent to $1.60 per barrel above Singapore spot quotes and gasoline at a $2.00-per-barrel premium to Singapote spot quotes, all on a c-and-f Chittagong basis.
Traders said Dutch oil trading firm Vitol Asia Pte Ltd made the next best offer under Group A.
Petco was awarded BPC's previous two tenders to buy oil products for July-December 1996 and January-June 1997 deliveries.
